data.title: When Will LULU Stock Hit Bottom? Asks Wells Fargo; Cuts Price Target on Weak Results
data.description:
Lululemon Athletica (LULU) stock plunged 20% in premarket trading after the athletic-apparel company reported weak second-quarter results and lowered its full-year outlook. With demand weakening and margins under pressure, Wells Fargo analyst Ike Boruchow is asking, "Where's the bottom?"

Boruchow cut his price target on LULU to $95 from $105, while maintaining a Hold rating. The new target implies nearly 22% downside from Thursday's closing price of $121.77. The premarket sell-off also pushed LULU stock to an 8-year low.

Lululemon reported a 4% year-over-year decline in second-quarter revenue to $2.4 billion, missing analysts' estimate of $2.46 billion. Comparable sales fell 9%, while sales in the Americas, the company's largest market, declined 8%.

Why Is Wells Fargo Worried About LULU Stock?

According to Boruchow, investors are now facing several challenges at the same time.

First, demand appears to be worsening. Lululemon has been struggling to maintain momentum in its core Americas business, with competition from brands such as Alo and Vuori adding pressure.

Second, weaker sales are creating fixed-cost deleverage. This means that when revenue falls, costs such as stores, employees and other fixed expenses do not decline at the same pace. As a result, profits can fall much faster than sales.

Third, Lululemon continues to rely on markdowns to move merchandise. Higher discounts can help clear inventory, but they also put pressure on profit margins.

Lululemon also received $134.5 million in tariff refunds and interest, adding $0.86 to quarterly EPS and boosting its gross margin by 5.6 percentage points. However, this benefit may not continue next year.

Could LULU Earnings Fall Below $6?

Boruchow's sees LULU's 2027 EPS falling to around $6.00 based on the current challenges, representing less than half of the earnings generated in the previous year.

The analyst believes that If Lululemon's earnings continue to fall, investors may be less willing to pay a premium for the stock. Lululemon has traditionally traded at a higher valuation because of its strong brand value, growth, and healthy profit margins.

New CEO Could Be the Biggest Catalyst

Lululemon's new CEO, former Nike (NKE) executive Heidi O'Neill, will take over on September 8 and focus on reviving North American sales and the brand. However, Boruchow does not expect investors to get immediate clarity.

He noted that the timeline for hearing from new management on its forward strategy could extend into next year. With limited visibility into the turnaround plan, he said he does not see a "credible Bull case for shares today."

Is Now a Good Time to Buy LULU Stock?

On TipRanks, LULU has a Hold consensus rating based on zero Buys, 19 Holds, and three Sell ratings. The average Lululemon Athletica price target of $102.67 implies 15.7% downside potential from current levels. Year-to-date, LULU shares have dropped 41.4%.
data.author: Sheryl Sheth

data.title: "Sell the News," Says GLJ Research Analyst as Tesla Stock Sinks After Cybercab Launch Backfires
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) shares are down over 6% on Friday after the EV giant's Cybercab robotaxi launch failed to meet investor expectations and immediately drew a federal safety audit. Following the event, GLJ Research analyst Gordon Johnson reiterated his Sell rating and $24.86 price target. Thus, the analyst concluded that the event was a "sell‑the‑news" moment, meaning it did not deliver enough to justify Tesla's recent run‑up.

On the regulatory front, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has opened a formal audit into nearly 1,000 Cybercabs. Since the two-seater vehicle lacks a steering wheel, pedals, or mirrors, it does not meet federal safety standards.

Here's Why the Analyst Is Disappointed With the Event

Johnson noted that Tesla offered no rollout target, no pricing, no consumer order option, no livestream, and no appearance from CEO Elon Musk. Instead, Tesla invited a group of friendly creators, who took short rides in a two‑seat robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals, then posted about it online.

According to state filings, only 45 Cybercabs were registered with the Texas DMV as of Wednesday, a number far below what bullish expectations had outlined. It must be noted that Alphabet's (GOOGL) Waymo already runs nearly 1,000 autonomous vehicles in the state, which makes Tesla's scale look very small in comparison.

Johnson argued that while engineering progress is real, the stock is priced for a full robotaxi network rather than a few cars in one city. He noted the disappointment came as Tesla's most supportive analysts had set a low bar for success and Tesla still came in below it.

For instance, Morgan Stanley had said 25-50 Cybercabs across Texas would likely push the stock higher, and that paid, unsupervised rides across multiple cities would represent a bullish outcome. Instead, Tesla showed one city, an unknown subset of 45 cars, and an app that did not let users request a ride as of Thursday night.

Is Tesla Stock Good to Buy Now?

Turning to Wall Street, TSLA stock has a Hold consensus rating based on 11 Buys, 14 Holds, and three Sells assigned in the past three months. The average price target for Tesla is $377.08, implying a 6.85% upside from the current price.

data.title: Micron Stock Faces Peak Risk by Late 2028 as Nvidia Budgets $267 Billion Memory Spend Through 2030
data.description:
Micron stock (MU) is facing a key risk. The risk is that its biggest buyer, Nvidia (NVDA), has only booked orders through 2030. Micron builds fast memory chips that pair with Nvidia processors to power AI models. Huge demand for these chips helped Micron stock surge 697% over the past year. However, if Nvidia buys fewer chips later, Micron stock's price run could end early.

Memory chip sales usually move in big ups and downs. While Micron stock trades near high levels, Nvidia's newest spending table gives investors a clear look at when this easy profit era might slow down.

Nvidia Budgets $267 Billion Memory Spend Through Fiscal 2030

Nvidia reported that its future order commitments grew from $119 billion to $279 billion, with most of that money going to memory chip makers like Micron, SK Hynix (SKHY), and Samsung (SSNLF).

Nvidia plans to spend $92 billion for the rest of Fiscal 2027, $87 billion in Fiscal 2028, and $88 billion in Fiscal 2029. This sets aside $267 billion for memory and supplies through January 2030. But in Fiscal 2030, Nvidia's booked orders fall to just $6 billion. Since memory chips are in short supply today, chipmakers make buyers sign multi-year deals, but Nvidia has not signed deals at today's high prices past 2029.

Should Micron Stock Investors Be Cautious?

Yes. Caution is advised. Nvidia's drop in booked orders from $88 billion down to $6 billion sets a trap for Micron stock investors. Micron will still ship memory chips through 2029 to fill older orders, which will keep its short-term sales reports looking strong.

However, stock markets like to look ahead. While Micron stock could keep rising through 2027 and 2028 on current sales, investors will not wait until 2030 to sell. If Nvidia does not sign new high-priced memory deals, markets could re-rate Micron stock between December 2028 and January 2029. This could lead to a price drop in MU stock.

Is Micron a Good Stock to Buy?

Turning to the Street, Micron stock carries a Strong Buy consensus based on 31 Buys and one Hold rating assigned in the past three months. The average 12-month MU stock price target is $1,554.67, which implies over 55.67% upside from the current price. (See MU stock forecast)

data.title: American Outdoor Brands Stock (AOUT) Surges More than 34% on Strong Q2 Growth
data.description:
American Outdoor Brands (AOUT) stock was up 34.67% on Friday after the outdoor gear and accessories company reported a strong start to fiscal 2027, with first-quarter revenue rising 25.4% to $37.3 million. The year-ago quarter had about $6 million in orders pulled forward by retailers, so sales rose 4.3% after removing that impact. Growth was broad across both Outdoor Lifestyle and Shooting Sports, as point-of-sale sales rose 6% in Outdoor Lifestyle and 3% in Shooting Sports.

Profit also improved as new products helped lift margins. Gross margin rose 630 basis points to 53.0%. GAAP net loss fell to $1.5 million from $6.8 million a year ago. On an adjusted basis, the company swung to $415,000 in net income from a $3.3 million loss. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $1.2 million from a $3.1 million loss. The company ended the quarter with $33.3 million in cash and no debt.

American Outdoor Brands noted that new products made up more than 36% of sales in the quarter. Caldwell's ClayCopter line saw strong demand and won the 2026 Frank Desomma Innovation of the Year award. Bubba also added new products, including its Pro Series Gen 2 Electric Fillet Knife. The company also launched Scoretracker Live with Major League Fishing, adding a digital service to Bubba's fishing gear. "We believe this approach has the potential to extend to other brands in our portfolio over time," said Brian Murphy, president and CEO of American Outdoor Brands.

American Outdoor Brands kept its full-year sales outlook at $200 million to $210 million but raised its adjusted EBITDA forecast to $14.5 million to $17.5 million. The company is now entering its stronger second and third quarters, with a focus on sales growth, profit gains and new product launches.

American Outdoor Brands stock was up 34.67% on Friday and has rallied 75.94% year-to-date. The stock has also increased 17.56% over the past 12 months.

data.title: Why Are Gold and Silver Down Today, 9/4/26?
data.description:
Both gold (XAUUSD) and silver (XAGUSD) are trading lower on Friday. Over the past 24 hours, gold and silver are down 1.41% and 2.02%, respectively. The precious metals faced pressure after August's jobs report showed nonfarm payrolls rising by 162,000 compared to expectations of 55,000. In addition, the unemployment rate remained unchanged at 4.1%.

With a strong labor market, the Fed is less likely to lower rates or hold them and more likely to raise them. However, gold and silver tend to underperform in a high-rate environment. That's because they don't generate interest, making the opportunity cost of holding them relative to interest-bearing assets greater.

Hike Odds Rise Ahead of Key Inflation Data Next Week

Following the jobs report, the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting climbed to 60.2% from 49.4% a day ago.
